name: Bo-Rukul
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

tone_statements.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2006 [this printout 29 Aug 2010]. The Rukul language of Central Nigeria and its affinities. Draft circulated for comment. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 25 pp.
tone_statements.quote: 3.3 Tones The tone system of Rukul is quite restricted, with only two tones. The majority of words appear all low tone. No cases of glide tones seem to occur. In most cases the tone is left unmarked. [...] [4.1 Nouns] In some rare cases, the tone is raised on an a- prefix, which has the effect of also raising the stem tone. [...] A few cases show the plural being made solely by stem tone-changes, with no functioning prefix. [...] [1. Introduction] In general, tones are not marked, although the data was taped and they will be added when time permits.
tone_statements.locator: Sec. 3.3 Tones, p. 3 (printed '-3-'); sec. 4.1 Nouns, pp. 5-6; Introduction p. 1 on unmarked tones

tone.says: Two-tone system described as 'quite restricted'; most words all-Low; no glide (contour) tones observed; tones mostly left unmarked in the 571-item list (data taped, marking deferred). Morphology notes tone raising on the a- noun prefix spreading to the stem and a few plurals formed solely by stem tone change (grammatical use of tone). No mention of stress or accent.
